title: Creative and Dramatic
blurb: Impressions, improv and doodles. For the group that likes to perform.

truth: What's the best character you've ever played in a school play or game?
Which celebrity would you like to be for a day?
What's the most dramatic thing you've done in real life?
What fictional role would you be perfect for?
What's a talent you'd love to be professional at?
What superhero name would you choose for yourself?
If you wrote a book, what would the title be?
What's the strangest costume you've ever worn?
What's your best impression, and who is it of?
If you had to give a TED talk tomorrow, what would it be about?
If you had your own TV show, what would it be called?
Who is your favourite comedian and why?
What's the best show or movie you've seen that made you want to act?
Which song would you choose as your walk-on music?
What's the most creative thing you've ever made?
If you could paint one thing, what would it be?
What's the most dramatic goodbye you've ever given?
What's a character trait you secretly share with a villain?
Which famous painting would you like on your wall?
If your life had a catchphrase, what would it be?
What's the funniest thing you've drawn?
What art form have you always wanted to try?
dare: Draw your best portrait of the person opposite you in 30 seconds and show everyone.
Act out a Shakespeare-style death scene for a small insect.
Do an impression of a famous person and have the group guess who.
Be a mime trapped in a box, then escape.
Speak in rhyme for the next two turns.
Act out a nature documentary about the group, with your best narrator voice.
Improvise a 20-second sales pitch for a pet rock.
Deliver a dramatic soap opera confession about the last biscuit.
Draw a monster with your non-writing hand and give it a name.
Pretend you are a statue of a famous person and hold the pose for 20 seconds.
Do a 15-second one-person play in which you are a door.
Do a movie-trailer voice-over for the story of someone's morning.
Create a new dance move and teach it to the group.
Sculpt something out of whatever is lying around, and present it as art.
Act out the same sentence in angry, sad and joyful styles.
Give a 20-second speech on why cats secretly rule the world.
Mime your favourite animal, charades style, until the group guesses it.
Narrate the room as if you're a fantasy epic storyteller.
Be a tree in a storm for ten seconds.
Draw a self-portrait without lifting your pen from the paper.
Act like a character who has just discovered fire.
Perform a 20-second stand-up routine about socks.
Do a freeze-frame of a famous painting and have the group guess it.
